message.content:
**Order filled:** 25 shares of COST at $905.00 = $22,625.00 (limit $905, filled at limit; quote was $904.13 bid / $904.15 ask, so the limit was ~0.1% above market). Remaining cash ≈ $27,375, no money moved out of the account, and the position is a buy in a permitted name.

**Summary:** I read Costco's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (year ended 2024-09-01) and checked the live quote ($904.13 last, $904.11/$904.15 bid-ask). The fundamentals support a purchase: net sales grew to $254,453M from $242,290M (+5.0%), operating income rose to $9,285M from $8,114M (+14.4%), net income to $7,367M from $6,292M (+17.1%), and operating cash flow was a healthy $11,339M — margin expansion on modest top-line growth, consistent with Costco's membership-fee model, and the filing notes ample liquidity for the next twelve months. I sized the order at 25 shares (~$22.6k) to stay under the $25,000 per-order cap and well within the $50,000 daily cap, using a limit of $905 (essentially the current market price) rather than a market order. One caveat worth flagging: the 10-K text includes a "Highlights" line stating fiscal 2024 diluted EPS of $17.39, but the trusted SEC-filing lookup reports **$16.56**; I used $16.56 in my key figures and did not rely on the $17.39 note. At $905 the shares trade at roughly 55x those reported diluted earnings — a rich multiple, so this is a small, quality-compounder starter position rather than a valuation-driven buy.
